parsedVerdict.reasoning: CatalogueService does use-case orchestration, which is the job of the application layer. It defines an input command DTO, checks through the injected ProductRepository port that a product ID is not already taken, and hands entity construction to the domain factory Product.create. It then saves the entity through the port and maps entities to snapshots for output. None of its code handles persistence directly (no SQL, file or storage access), transport (no HTTP or request/response handling) or framework concerns. It does not reimplement entity business rules: validation of product data is assumed to sit inside Product.create in the domain. The duplicate-ID check is a use-case precondition that needs the repository, so it reasonably belongs in the application layer. No ADR prose was provided.
